anya: Heads-up: seeing OOMs on prod-heavy-run after the attn-kernel swap. Repro locally with seq=4096, batch=8. Heap is churning and we hit OOMs intermittently. Dropping logs below.

 tom_k: Can you paste the logs / knobs?

 anya: Current allocator knobs on the runner:
 ```
 expandable_segments = true
 max_split_size_mb = 32
 garbage_collection_threshold = 0.8
 workspace_reserve_mb = 128
 ```
 Example error snippet:
 ```
 RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 276824064 bytes (263.7 MB)
 Allocations: split_count=412, avg_segment=24MB, free_small_blks=~150
 ```

 liam: Sounds like fragmentation + lots of small frees. Did you run torch.cuda.memory_summary or a pmap of allocations? Could also be kv-cache churn. :thinking:

 anya: Yes - memory_summary shows many short-lived 16-48MB chunks. pmap tracing shows allocator doing frequent splits. Repro script: https://internal/repro/attn-oom-4096 (private)

 tom_k: Quick try: increase max_split_size_mb -> 128 and set expandable_segments=false to prefer larger contiguous segments. Also try lowering GC threshold to 0.6 so GC happens earlier.

 anya: Ran that locally just now. Results: before change 1 OOM / 5 runs; after change 0 OOM / 20 runs. Cold-start latency +3-6ms but stability improved. Memory headroom ~+120MB on steady-state.

 liam: Nice. I suspect the new attn kernel allocates a relatively big temporary workspace each call; when allocator keeps splitting small segments the workspace can't land contiguously. Increasing max_split_size and reserving workspace helps. Try bumping workspace_reserve_mb to 256 to keep a warm slab for those temp ws.

 anya: Bumped workspace_reserve_mb=256. Tracing shows reuse_rate up from 46% -> 81% and split_count down ~60%. OOMs stopped.

 infra-bot: ci-build/4567 finished: perf-infra tests ✅ (smoketest passed)

 tom_k: Let's prepare a canary with defaults changed to: max_split_size_mb=128, expandable_segments=false, garbage_collection_threshold=0.6, workspace_reserve_mb=256. Include a fallback: if a single allocation request > max_split_size_mb then allow expandable_segments to avoid regressions on huge-single-alloc workloads.

 anya: I'll open a PR with the default changes + changelog + the safe-fallback. Also adding telemetry metrics: allocator.split_count and allocator.reuse_rate (percent).

 liam: One more suggestion: add a debug flag to log when splits happen > N times per request so we can alert before OOM. Also add a short guidance blurb in ops-runbook about these knobs and the kernel-change interaction.

 deploy-bot: starting staging deploy: canary group=21 (eta ~8m)

 tom_k: Great. If staging looks good we flip the defaults and roll to prod canary. Document rationale and link the perf traces in the PR. :thumbsup:

 anya: Will do. Thanks all. :party_parrot:
